title: Project
text: This ILTER-funded project aims to collect tree-ring data of Ulmus laevis across its distribution range throughout Europe. The initial survey addressed approximately 400 managers of potential ILTER sites. However, the project is open to all interested researchers, forestry practitioners, nature conservationists, and others.

title: Project
text:
Background
Ulmus laevis is an understudied tree species in dendroecology and forest management. Unlike Ulmus glabra and Ulmus minor, which were heavily affected by Dutch elm disease, U. laevis appears comparatively resilient. However, large-scale analyses of its growth and climate sensitivity are lacking.

title: Project
text:
Goals
ElmNET aims to compile a large-scale tree-ring dataset to assess the growth, vitality, and climate sensitivity of U. laevis across Europe and to identify macroclimatic and microclimatic growth differences.

title: Participation
text:
We actively welcome further collaborations and data contributions to improve the spatial coverage and representativeness of the dataset.
At least 15 sampled trees per site are required, ideally accompanied by metadata and stand information.
Pre-measured tree-ring data are preferred, but tree cores are equally valuable. Contributions from unusual sites, for example particularly dry stands, are especially welcome.
